cards.title: Brief
cards.description: Emperor: goal, users, stories, measurable outcome
cards.prompt:
Turn the confirmed hypothesis into a product brief: goal, users, key stories, measurable outcome.

Do not start implementation. If validation never passed, say so and recommend the Validation deck.

Output: goal · users · stories · success metric · constraints.

cards.title: MVP
cards.description: Two of Swords: IN / OUT, one happy path, acceptance
cards.prompt:
Freeze MVP: IN / OUT, one happy path, acceptance criteria, deferred features.

YAGNI: cut anything not needed for the first real user path. No code.

cards.title: Interface
cards.description: Ace of Cups: screens, buttons, empty/error/loading
cards.prompt:
Describe screens, controls, empty/loading/error states, and navigation in text.

Do not generate image/figma files unless the user asked. Keep it implementable.

cards.title: Données
cards.description: Ace of Pentacles: entities only if the project needs them
cards.prompt:
Define entities, validation, storage, and external contracts ONLY if this project needs them.

Do not invent a database, REST API, Prisma, or tRPC for a local/desktop app that does not need them. If none needed, say so and list what is stored where.

cards.title: Architecture
cards.description: Chariot: simplest fit after reading the repo
cards.prompt:
Read the repo and existing dependencies first. Propose the simplest structure and stack that fits.

Record risks and a rollback idea. Prefer boring working software over a fashionable architecture.

cards.title: Règles
cards.prompt:
Inspect existing AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules/*.mdc. Propose the smallest non-conflicting updates.

Do not create a legacy .cursorrules file by default. Do not duplicate rules already written. Ask before writing files if the user did not request edits.

cards.title: Revue
cards.prompt:
Review the specification for clarity, completeness, YAGNI, safety, and testability.

Project quality score 0–10: below 7 must be fixed before coding.

Always end with this exact line (N = 0-10):
KEYCODE_SCORE: N

If score < 7, name the one spec card that should run next.

cards.title: Prêt ?
cards.description: Judgement: gate to Hobby or Production work
cards.prompt:
Check that goal, scope, UX, needed contracts, architecture, acceptance, and rollback exist.

Do not guess Hobby vs Production if the user has not chosen.

End with:
KEYCODE_GATE: PASS
KEYCODE_NEXT: lazy-v1/plan

or (if they already chose production):
KEYCODE_GATE: PASS
KEYCODE_NEXT: pro-v1/plan

or:
KEYCODE_GATE: FAIL
KEYCODE_NEXT: spec-v1/brief

(replace brief with the one missing spec card id if you know it).

cards.title: Récap
cards.description: High Priestess: hypothesis / evidence / gaps / next
cards.prompt:
Read this chat. Do not write or change code.

Four short blocks:
1. Goal
2. Decided
3. Open
4. Next step (name a Specification card, or Work · Hobby / Work · Production)

No KEYCODE_SCORE / GATE / NEXT lines.
